scope_rule: All actual first-party embedded PHP algorithms and runtime outcomes remain in the Rust completion goal. Zend ABI/value/refcount/GC/exception/bailout/VM and required OS effects may use minimal native shims, after Rust returns. This does not exempt pool/retry/RPC/proxy/collection/coordination policy.
reservation_effect: None. Existing owners, frozen ABI and unavailable areas remain protected. Planning anchors are scope assignments, never implementation grants or new capacity.
conditional_profiles: enable_library on/off and CLI RINIT versus preloader
Actual enabled hook flags, coroutine context and installed builtin availability
Native curl versus PHP coroutine curl emulation; sockets extension on/off
Optional PDO/database/Redis/MongoDB services and driver availability
PHP supported versions, ZTS/NTS and actual thread operational capability
external_dependencies: Retain mature vendor drivers/crypto/parsers only as separately declared dependencies; first-party policy around them remains in scope.
known_evidence_gaps: The actual embedded functions.php differs semantically from companion revision26e2e98; companion source is not an interchangeable oracle.
Database originals with missing singular example paths remain unavailable until provenance/setup is closed.
Literal references and hook edges are candidates, not proof that originals execute every payload.
Original exec/shell_exec names do not establish a route to embedded swoole_exec helpers.
Full feature/platform union and runtime qualification remain incomplete.
